artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(F_n)_{n\ge 0}$ be the Fibonacci sequence defined by $F_0=0$, $F_1=1$, $F_{n+1}=F_n+F_{n-1}$, and let $(L_n)_{n\ge 0}$ be the Lucas sequence defined by $L_0=2$, $L_1=1$, $L_{n+1}=L_n+L_{n-1}$. For an odd prime $p\ne 5$, let $\left(\tfrac{p}{5}\right)$ denote the Legendre symbol, and define the Fibonacci–Fermat quotient
$$q := \frac{F_{p-\left(\frac{p}{5}\right)}}{p}\in\mathbb Z.$$
Prove or disprove the following four congruences modulo $p^2$:
\begin{align*}
p\sum_{k=1}^{p-1}\frac{F_{2k}}{k^2\binom{2k}{k}} &\equiv -\left(\tfrac{p}{5}\right)\!\left(\tfrac32 q+\tfrac{5}{4}p\,q^2\right)\pmod{p^2},\\
p\sum_{k=1}^{p-1}\frac{L_{2k}}{k^2\binom{2k}{k}} &\equiv -\tfrac52 q-\tfrac{15}{4}p\,q^2\pmod{p^2},\\
\sum_{k=0}^{(p-3)/2}\frac{\binom{2k}{k}F_{2k+1}}{(2k+1)\,16^k} &\equiv (-1)^{(p+1)/2}\left(\tfrac{p}{5}\right)\!\left(\tfrac12 q+\tfrac{5}{8}p\,q^2\right)\pmod{p^2},\\
\sum_{k=0}^{(p-3)/2}\frac{\binom{2k}{k}L_{2k+1}}{(2k+1)\,16^k} &\equiv (-1)^{(p+1)/2}\!\left(\tfrac52 q+\tfrac{5}{8}p\,q^2\right)\pmod{p^2}.
\end{align*}

artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture appears in Z.-W. Sun's collection of open conjectures on congruences (last revised 2019). A web search did not return any published proof of these four supercongruences modulo $p^2$ involving Fibonacci/Lucas numbers, central binomial coefficients, and the Fibonacci–Fermat quotient. Related results by Z.-H. Sun and others address similar but distinct congruences, leaving the stated identities apparently still open.

status_evidence.snippet: Collection of about 100 open conjectures on congruences, including Conjecture A90 on sums involving F_{2k}, L_{2k}, central binomial coefficients, and the Fibonacci–Fermat quotient.

status_evidence.snippet: Studies congruences modulo p^2 involving Lucas sequences and central binomial coefficients, but does not establish the four identities of Conjecture A90.
